subject: Post-demo: cost targets & continuous-batching assumptions
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@finlytics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo notes: cost targets & batching assumptions

Hi Samira / Rajiv — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and the asks we agreed to: 

Summary from today's call:
- Your primary goal: integrate a 1st-party analytics assistant into Finlytics' workflow for quarterly reports. Expected peak QPS during report generation windows.
- Target latency: interactive for analysts (~300ms median gen latency end-to-end) for short queries, longer for long multi-turn generations.
- Budget guidance: SigOps mentioned a target of ~$900–1,200 per 1M tokens for a workable POC (before discounts/commit). You flagged this as a critical gating metric.

What we need to validate (action items):
1) Token-volume profile: you offered to share a sample week of traffic (typical prompt lengths, average generated tokens per request, peak vs baseline). We'll use that to simulate unit econ. (Rajiv: sample CSV please)
2) Batching & concurrency expectations: you expect continuous-batching during report windows (steady stream of short prompts from many analysts) rather than large single-batch jobs. Confirmed concurrency target: 40–120 concurrent real-user requests during peak. We will model both continuous small-batch and occasional bursts.
3) Cost target: We will run a sensitivity analysis aiming for your target $/1M tokens with our recommended quantization + batching profile; we'll show tradeoffs (latency vs $).

Attachments: attached a short econ deck and a CSV template for your traffic export.

Next steps / timeline:
- Rajiv: share the traffic sample by Wed 3/17.
- Redwood (Dev & Marissa): return a token-unit-econ spreadsheet + recommended batching/concurrency profile by Tue 3/23.
- Samira: confirm if SOC2 evidence will be required for POC later this month.

If that matches, we'll slot a 30-min follow-up to walk the numbers next week.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: 2027-03-15_finlytics-econ-deck.pdf (PDF, 6 slides)

From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@finlytics.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 18:06:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo notes: cost targets & batching assumptions

Thanks Evelyn — quick reply while I pull the export. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The ~1,200 per 1M tokens number was our internal acceptable ceiling for the first month of POC. We can be flexible if latency/UX is excellent.
- Token distribution: median prompt ~35 tokens, median generated ~120 tokens; but a long-tail of heavier jobs when analysts generate full narratives.
- Concurrency: 40 typical during working hours; up to ~150 for day-of-report spikes (these are short lived, ~5–10min). Continuous-batching model sounds right for steady periods.

I'll send a 7-day sample CSV by EOD Wed (17th). Also open to a short calc call to align assumptions.

—Rajiv
Director, Product Engineering, Finlytics

Subject: RE: Post-demo notes: cost targets & batching assumptions — internal tech checklist

Eve / Marissa — internal notes after the demo and Rajiv's reply: 

1) Assumptions to model in the econ sheet:
   - Model A (latency-priority): continuous batching with small windows (20–50ms batching threshold), concurrency 40–60; expect ~15–25% token-cost reduction from continuous prefix caching; target cost to show: $1,200/1M tokens.
   - Model B (cost-priority): increase batching window to 80–120ms and admit slightly higher P95 latency; concurrency 40–120; expected cost delta ~25–40% lower than Model A depending on model/quantization. Aim to show $700–900/1M tokens with mixed int8 quantization.

2) Workload modelling notes:
   - Use the raw-traffic-samples.csv; key columns: timestamp, prompt_tokens, gen_tokens, user_id, request_type. We'll simulate arrival as Poisson with peak multipliers for spike windows.
   - For continuous batching: implement steady-state batching logic where we flush every 25ms or when batch size reaches 32 (whichever first). Simulate KV cache hit rates (60–85%) for short follow-ups.

3) Deliverables & owners:
   - Dev: run sims and produce unit-econ table + sensitivity rows (latency, batch window, concurrency). Due Tue 3/23 EOD.
   - Marissa: draft the POC SOW snippet with the cost assumptions and SLA options. Due Tue 3/23 EOD.

I'll start the sim run with a baseline LlamaX-34B fp16 profile then run quantized variants.

-Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
